searchText: <@884836500037066862> <@586161934425128960> Sorry guys. I was OOO all of last week. Yes, what you've described is accurate. I'm open to accepting same-epoch proposer preferences but I still think we should disallow it. These preferences are only necessary to receive builder bids for more MEV income. If a validator were to be offline until the epoch of their proposal, I think the node should just self-build and propose that. If we allow same-slot preferences, I might cause a bunch of re-orgs if an attacker repeatedly sends preferences just before their proposal slot. interested in nico's opinion, maybe when making the beacon api spec we just allow current epoch to go through without broadcasting setting local caches to replace /eth/v1/validator/prepare_beacon_proposer and next epoch actually broadcasts it? if we don't want to allow it for current epoch? > These preferences are only necessary to receive builder bids for more MEV income I don't like this argument, we are moving towards making local building unfeasible so the trustless builder path should be as robust as possible can't we just add a gossip check which states that `proposal_slot` of the proposer preference needs to be before current slot? Note that, we will likely deprecate validator registrations in the builder-api too and require builders to listen to proposer preferences gossip topic for info like gas limit etc. i think this check makes sense to me. so that clients can rebroadcast the proposer preferences Do we really want to deal with these edge cases? I mean c'mon if you're so unlucky you should build locally anyway in these cases you will still get bids and you may like them anyway I don't think we should change the protocol to deal with these severe edge cases that pose no risk to the chain at all I haven't looked at the implemention yet but this extra restriction to only allow them to be broadcast for next epoch makes things more complext, not simpler, maybe <@884836500037066862> can speak more to that I mean if the change is to simply allow preferences to be broadcast for current epoch and next epoch it's absolutely fine. We're not adding a larger DOS surface at all But in general the theme of changing protocol to deal with these types of edge cases seems ridiculous to me not per spec right now > If a validator does not broadcast a > `SignedProposerPreferences` message, this implies that the validator will not > accept any trustless bids for that slot. and I think it's fine to keep this note I think this is arbitrarily brittle: any network participant that hasn't seen the preference for any reason, will not be propagating bids that can help liveness there's no reason to stop information from flowing the proposer can always decide to drop them anyway I mean ideally we use this chance to get rid of eth/v1/validator/prepare_beacon_proposer, i proposed above if we want to avoid broadcasting if when we have a beacon api spec we allow it being called just for the purposes of local building if we hit that edge case? not against that, we can drop them at application layer instead of gossip easily we can but it seems simpler if we could have both local cache and gossip propagation to be more aligned I think these edge cases happen more regularly than maybe someone would initially think, we've gone through a lot of bugs and iterations on the validator registration and prepare beacon proposer endpoints and if we want to get rid of those 2 in favor of this one I just want those edge cases to be covered it'd still be best effort, if you're broadcasting while building is happening you're outa luck - but yeh to potuz's point i dont think the protocol needs to restrict that per-say. I don't think starting up and proposing in that first epoch should be considered an 'edge case' really, but it fits this scenario. probably no point broadcasting if we're already in that slot, but for future slots it makes sense... arguably 'next slot' would be potentially 'too late'?

excerpts.author: jtraglia
excerpts.content: <@884836500037066862> <@586161934425128960> Sorry guys. I was OOO all of last week. Yes, what you've described is accurate. I'm open to accepting same-epoch proposer preferences but I still think we should disallow it. These preferences are only necessary to receive builder bids for more MEV income. If a validator were to be offline until the epoch of their proposal, I think the node should just self-build and propose that. If we allow same-slot preferences, I might cause a bunch of re-orgs if an attacker repeatedly sends preferences just before their proposal slot.

excerpts.author: jameshe5018
excerpts.content: interested in nico's opinion, maybe when making the beacon api spec we just allow current epoch to go through without broadcasting setting local caches to replace /eth/v1/validator/prepare_beacon_proposer and next epoch  actually broadcasts it? if we don't want to allow it for current epoch?

excerpts.author: nflaig
excerpts.content:
> These preferences are only necessary to receive builder bids for more MEV income
I don't like this argument, we are moving towards making local building unfeasible so the trustless builder path should be as robust as possible

excerpts.author: nflaig
excerpts.content: can't we just add a gossip check which states that `proposal_slot` of the proposer preference needs to be before current slot?

excerpts.author: bharath.vedartham
excerpts.content: Note that, we will likely deprecate validator registrations in the builder-api too and require builders to listen to proposer preferences gossip topic for info like gas limit etc.

excerpts.author: bharath.vedartham
excerpts.content: i think this check makes sense to me. so that clients can rebroadcast the proposer preferences
